items.title: Theranos.world
items.author: kbyatnal
items.summary: Theranos was a company that attracted significant attention and investment, reaching a valuation of over $9 billion and forming partnerships with the Cleveland Clinic and Walgreens. However, it faced legal troubles culminating in Elizabeth Holmes's conviction for defrauding investors in January 2022. Theranos had also received a $100 million loan from Fortress Investment Group in December 2017 to stave off bankruptcy, but ultimately laid off most of its workforce in April 2018 in another attempt to avoid bankruptcy. The sources don't provide a definitive answer to the current status of Theranos.

items.title: Man discovers his parents' coffee machine used 1TB of data in 10 days
items.author: ck2
items.summary: A techie discovered that his parents' smart coffee machine, a Keurig model, used 1TB of data in just 10 days. The techie, who has over a decade of experience in IT, found that most of the data stayed within the home network rather than being sent over the internet. He concluded that the massive data usage was likely due to a bug in the coffee machine. The techie shared his findings on social media, leading to the decision to buy his parents a new coffee maker.

items.title: AI-ready biological data: $1.8B global commitment
items.author: ray__
items.summary: Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health, and new funding partners announced a major expansion of an international effort to generate and make accessible AI-ready biological data, committing $1.8 billion in funding, data, computation, and new measurement technology. This initiative, known as the Virtual Biology Initiative, aims to coordinate data generation across institutions and disciplines to build AI-ready open datasets to enable predictive models of life. Biohub’s founding $500 million commitment anchors that work, with $400 million supporting new technologies that expand what biologists can measure. The US government and tech heavyweights Meta Platforms and Google parent Alphabet are also joining the effort, bringing the total investment to $1.8 billion.

items.title: Show HN: Jevman – AI decision models play Pac-Man
items.author: felix089
items.text:
Openai just launched their decisions endpoint, cloudflare launched clef the other week, and many more jev alternatives are out there.

We wanted to put the popular ones to the test and thought Pac-Man is a good benchmark for simple and fast decision making.

So we let jev 1.13, kev, clef, clef flash, GPT-6 Luna and Laya play Pac-Man against bot ghosts.

The low latency of these models allows for real time play. We had each model play 100 games, published a leader board and open-sourced the re
items.summary: Jevman is an AI benchmark where various AI decision models, including jev 1.13, kev, clef, clef flash, GPT-6 Luna, and Laya, play Pac-Man against arcade ghosts. Each model played 100 games, and the leaderboard ranks them based on their performance. The low latency of these models allows for real-time play, and the repo is open-sourced for anyone to run their own model and join the ranking. The benchmark tests simple and fast decision-making through playing Pac-Man.

items.title: OpenAI withdraws three mathematical results
items.author: sashank_1509
items.summary: On October 7, 2026, OpenAI withdrew three of its 722 AI-generated math manuscripts due to a sign error in a proof related to Weil-classes, which also affected two dependent papers. The company has yet to specify if more retractions will follow from the remaining unverified results. The error was flagged by the company's own repository, not through peer review. Currently, about 42 percent of the posted results have formalized proofs in Lean, a programming language for checking mathematical proofs.

items.title: I think I found a planet nobody knew existed. I used Claude Code to find it
items.author: pyduan
items.summary: According to the sources, a Reddit user claims to have found a planet using Claude Code, which led to NASA pointing a telescope at it for confirmation. The planet is described as a 1.4× Earth-size candidate located 116 light-years away, dimming its star every 3.18 days. The signal has appeared in observations from 2018, 2020, and 2025, and follow-up TESS time was approved. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the planet's official status or confirmation.

items.title: 15-year search for a band that charted once and vanished
items.author: shahidhussain
items.summary: The sources mention a band called Crustation that released a single trip-hop album featuring Irish vocalist Bronagh Slevin and charted at #47 on the UK Independent Singles Chart in June 2006. The author of the Hacker News post spent 15 years trying to uncover more about the band, but found no online credits, fingerprint match, company registration, or streaming presence. The band vanished after their single, and their website was Flash-based, which contributed to their lack of online presence. The other sources mention bands like Men at Work, Ram Jam, and Paper Lace that had significant success but then disappeared, but none specifically match the 15-year search for Crustation.

items.title: Show HN: TerrainSR – fast, realistic heightmap upscaling model
items.author: joegibbs
items.text:
This is a model that I made for a historical game. I wanted to have a 1:1 scale model of Europe, but my problem was that 100m data was too low-res while 10m LIDAR data was patchy, took hundreds of GBs to store and was full of manmade objects like mines, buildings and so on.

I trained this model on undeveloped landscape so that it can quickly add plausible erosion features, rocks, etc to the low-resolution height data and sort of reconstruct what the terrain would look like before any human int
items.summary: TerrainSR is a model that allows you to generate realistic higher-detail terrain height data from lower-detail terrain height data. It is trained on 100m -> 10m pairs and is faster and more varied than using a traditional erosion simulator for large terrains. On an RTX 4070, TerrainSR generates a 50x50km patch from 100m to 10m in 0.74s, making it applicable for realtime applications such as gaming. The model is available on Hugging Face and GitHub, where it is compared to other upscaling models in terms of speed and performance.

items.title: Anger as man sentenced to death for Facebook comment
items.author: bcaulfield
items.summary: Anojan Sivarasa, a 24-year-old Sri Lankan migrant worker, was sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia for a Facebook comment deemed insulting to Islam and Prophet Muhammad. Initially sentenced to five years in prison and fined 3 million Saudi riyals, his sentence was later appealed and changed to the death penalty. His family has pleaded for mercy, and Amnesty International has condemned the sentence, highlighting concerns about the application of the death penalty and the arbitrariness of the Saudi criminal justice system. The case underscores severe concerns regarding severe sentences for online speech in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: OpenAI annualised revenues $20B less than previously signalled
items.author: mfiguiere
items.summary: According to the Financial Times, the discrepancy in OpenAI's annualized revenue arose from differences in how investors calculated its revenue. The company had previously told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $70 billion, but recent reports suggest it is closer to $50 billion. This difference does not indicate a loss in sales but rather reflects varying methods of revenue calculation, particularly in how revenue from sales via cloud partners like AWS and Google Cloud is included.

items.title: Sub-1-Bit LLM Compression via Latent Factorization
items.author: brainless
items.summary: The sources indicate that sub-1-bit LLM compression via latent factorization has been explored through frameworks like LittleBit and NanoQuant. LittleBit achieves extreme compression with a memory reduction of approximately 31× and a new size-performance trade-off, enabling an 11.6× inference speedup relative to FP16. NanoQuant proposes a post-training quantization method that compresses LLMs to binary and sub-1-bit levels through low-rank binary factorization, establishing a new Pareto frontier in low-memory post-training quantization. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on specific details beyond these frameworks and their achievements.
